hypothesis: The newly published discovery page should remain readable and technically accessible on simulated mobile before more content or speculative performance changes.
action: Ran documented Lighthouse 12.8.2 public-page audit in temporary Chrome profile; checked response latency with three sequential public GETs.

audits.title: Browser errors were logged to the console

decision: No speculative source change: good mobile lab result, slow initial Lighthouse response not reproduced in bounded GET sample. Existing platform-injected inline-script CSP error does not justify relaxing script policy.
limits: One simulated mobile lab navigation, not field Core Web Vitals or customer usability proof.
Three GETs are a tiny same-location sample, not global latency or a cold/warm causal experiment.
Lighthouse SEO score is not Google indexing, ranking, traffic or AI citation evidence.
No source changes, deployment, customer requests, inference, email, payments, purchase or new controller.
followUp: After a material page/platform change or real incident, compare same tool/version and metrics. On/after 21 October measure bounded discovery including the new page; next genuine guide request measure independently reviewed usefulness.

supervisorVerification.method: Read-only comparison with retained temporary Lighthouse JSON
supervisorVerification.latencyControls: Controller-recorded three public GETs; no independent rerun
supervisorVerification.boundary: One simulated lab navigation only; no field performance, usability, indexing, citation or conversion proof
